walkthroughs.body_html:
Energetics — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Energetics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Energetics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which reaction has ΔH = ΔH_f° as defined?
options: 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l)
H₂(g) + ½O₂(g) → H₂O(l)
H₂O(l) → H₂(g) + ½O₂(g)
H₂O(g) → H₂O(l)
Positive ΔH
Negative ΔH
ΔH = 0
Variable ΔH

mcqs.q: In an exothermic reaction, what happens energetically with the bonds?
options: Energy released forming new bonds exceeds energy absorbed breaking existing bonds.
Bond breaking releases energy and bond making absorbs energy.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.

mcqs.q: What does a mole of a substance represent?
options: A mole is a unit of mass equal to the relative molecular mass in grams of any substance.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
Avogadro's number (6.02 x 10^23) of particles of that substance.

mcqs.q: At room temperature and pressure, what volume does 1 mole of any gas occupy?
options: The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
Approximately 24 dm^3 (24,000 cm^3), regardless of the identity of the gas.
Heavier gases occupy a smaller volume per mole because their particles are denser.
